text.p: The International Committee of the Red Cross escorted 45 prisoners of war to rump Yugoslavia on Thursday after they were freed by Croatia.
Croatia released the 45 men under provisions of an expanded war amnesty for Serbs who fought in a minority rebellion prompted by Zagreb's 1991 move to independence from old Yugoslavia.

An ICRC spokeswoman said the detainees were transported from the Obonjan, Varazdin and Dugo Selo collection centres in Croatia via the Bajakovo border crossing to Belgrade, the Yugoslav capital, where they were welcomed by several hundred relatives.
"They have crossed into Yugoslavia," Gordana Milenkovic of the ICRC office in Belgrade told Reuters.

Before the release, ICRC delegates carried out private interviews with the released detainees, she said. The men had the choice to stay in Croatia or to be reunited with their relatives in Yugoslavia.
Some 40 released detainees chose to remain in Croatia, she said.
The 45 men who arrived in Yugoslavia on Thursday evening were detained by the Croatian army when it recaptured Krajina region last August.
The ICRC has transferred 434 released detainees from Croatia to Yugoslavia since 1995. Croatia still holds some 120 detainees, according to Belgrade authorities.
Croatia and rump Yugoslavia signed a diplomatic normalisation treaty two months ago, ending five years of hostility.
